full_judgment: 9. The learned Advocate has also drawn our attention to certain cases of the Indian jurisdiction of which two decisions are of the Calcutta High Court, namely, the case of Padri Prasad Jhunjhunwalla Vs. Rabulal Jhunjhunwalla and others, reported in A.I.R. 1950 Cal. 368 and the case of Premraj Mundra Vs. Md. Maneck Gazi and others reported in A.I.R. 1951 Cal 156. In Badriprasad's case a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court, has taken the view that an order of attachment before judgment passed without consoling with the provision of Order 38. rule 5 and 6 of the Code, was not necessarily ultra vires or void ab initio. In the said case, the High Court set aside an order of attachment before judgment but maintained the conditional order of attachment. In the other Calcutta case, which is a Single Judge decision, it has been held that on an application made under Order 38 rule 5 and 6 of the Code, the Court should come to a decision as to whether prima facie the defendants have reasonable chance of success at the trial and whether the plaintiff's case that the defendants were transferring their property with an intention to delay or defeat the plaintiff's claim is correct. On the facts of that case the learned Judge has held that defendant actually made an attempt to leave the country after selling his property from India and that the order of attachment under Order 38 rule 5 was property made. The learned Advocate has also referred to a decision of the Patna High Court in the case of Md. Ali Ismail Vs. Baldeo Singh, reported in A.I.R. 1955 Pat. 115 which relied upon the decision reported in A.I.R. 1950 Cal. page 368. In the said Patna case, the learned Judges have taken the view that non-compliance with rule 5 of the Order 38 of the Code was an irregularity and that such an irregularity can be waked by the defendant.
